plain: Able to be done in practice

webster.text: That may be done, effected or performed by human means, or by powers that can be applied.

more.text: That may be practiced; as a practicable virtue.

example.quote: But if the legislature of the Union can not do all the good that might be wished, it is at least desirable that all may be done which is practicable.
example.cite: Alexander Hamilton, Report on Manufactures (communicated to the House of Representatives, Dec. 5, 1791)
